name: Saint John of the Cross
bio_en: John of the Cross (1542–1591) was a Spanish Carmelite, mystic, and Doctor of the Church, known for his teaching on the spiritual path of purification and union with God.

name: Saint Mariam of Jesus Crucified
bio_en: Mariam of Jesus Crucified (1846–1878), also known as Mariam Baouardy, was a Palestinian Carmelite, mystic, and stigmatist, venerated for her humility and extraordinary gifts of grace.
bio_en_long:
Mariam Baouardy was born on 5 January 1846 in Ibillin, in Upper Galilee, into a poor, faith led, Eastern Christian family. After her parents lost twelve boys in infancy, Mariam was born to them thanks to a pilgrimage to Bethlehem. Two years later, her brother Boulos was born, but at three years old she lost both her parents and was entrusted to a paternal uncle, who later moved to Alexandria. 
 From a very young age, she was marked by a profound spiritual sensitivity, perceiving the eeting nature of life and an invitation to give her heart to God. Not yet 13 years old, she refused an arranged marriage, desiring to consecrate herself entirely to Christ. Mistreated by her uncle, she went to see a former servant of her uncle who pressured her to convert to Islam. She refused, proclaiming her Christian faith. The servant slit her throat and abandoned her in a dark alley. Mariam awoke in a cave, cared for by a woman dressed in blue, whom she would later identify as the Virgin Mary. One woman then led her to a church and left her there. Mariam began to work as a servant for families in Alexandria, Jerusalem, Beirut, and then Marseille, where, in 1865, she entered the Sisters of Saint Joseph of the Apparition. Soon, her mystical gifts began to appear: visions, ecstasies, stigmata, and prophecies. After two years of novitiate, Mariam was not permitted to profess vows. 
 In June 1867, she joined the Carmel of Pau, France, as a lay sister and took the name Sister Mary of Jesus Crucified. Little and unassuming, she devoted herself to manual labor even as she experienced her mystical gifts with humility. In 1870, she departed for India to help found the Carmel of Mangalore, where she accomplished her work with self-denial. She professed her vows at the end of her novitiate on 21 November 1871. However, misunderstandings related to the manifestations of her mystical gifts began to arise around her, casting doubt on the authenticity of what she was experiencing. The resulting tensions finally led to her being sent back to the Carmel of Pau, France, in 1872. She was warmly welcomed there. There she returned to her simple life as a lay sister amid the affection of her sisters.
 In 1875, after many obstacles, she founded the Carmel of Bethlehem. The Lord revealed to her both the location and the construction plans. She supervised the construction thanks to her knowledge of Arabic. She also contributed to the acquisition of land for the future Carmel of Nazareth. While carrying water to the construction workers at the Carmel of Bethlehem, she fell and was seriously injured; gangrene led to her death on 26 August 1878. Her life, marked by humility, service, and mystical experiences, makes her a witness to the invisible universe of faith.

name: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux
bio_en: Thérèse of Lisieux (1873–1897), a Carmelite and Doctor of the Church, taught the “Little Way” of trust and love and is one of the most popular saints of modern times.

name: Father Jacques of Jesus
bio_en: Father Jacques of Jesus (1900–1945), a Carmelite and French priest, hid Jewish children during the Second World War, was arrested, and died shortly after the liberation of a concentration camp.

name: Saint Teresa of the Andes
bio_en: Teresa of the Andes (1900–1920) was a Chilean Carmelite who became known from a young age for her deep love of Christ and her devotion to life in the convent.

name: The Saints of Carmel
bio_en: The saints of Carmel include a great multitude of men and women who attained holiness in the spirit of Mary of Mount Carmel through contemplation, sacrifice, and service to the Church.

name: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus
Saint Teresa of Ávila
bio_en: Teresa of Ávila (1515–1582) was a Spanish mystic, reformer of Carmel, and Doctor of the Church whose spiritual writings and convent reforms profoundly shaped Western spirituality.

name: Mary of the Incarnation
bio_en: Sister Mary of the Incarnation was a Carmelite whose spirituality focused particularly on the mystery of Christ’s Incarnation and invited people to contemplate God made man.

name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
bio_en: Our Lady of Mount Carmel is a Marian title referring to the biblical Mount Carmel. She is venerated as the patroness of the Carmelite Order and is associated with the scapular.

name: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein)
bio_en: Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein, 1891–1942) was a philosopher of Jewish heritage who converted to the Catholic faith, became a Carmelite, and died as a martyr in Auschwitz concentration camp.

name: Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection
bio_en: Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection (1614–1691) was a French Carmelite lay brother known for his teaching on the constant presence of God in everyday life.

name: Saint Joseph
bio_en: Saint Joseph, husband of the Virgin Mary and foster father of Jesus, is venerated as the silent just man and faithful protector of the Church and families.

name: Saint Elisabeth of the Trinity
bio_en: Elisabeth of the Trinity (1880–1906) was a French Carmelite whose spirituality was shaped by the indwelling presence of the Most Holy Trinity in the heart of the baptized person.

name: Blessed Marie-Eugène of the Child Jesus OCD
bio_en: Marie-Eugène of the Child Jesus (1894–1967) was a French Carmelite and founder of the secular institute Notre-Dame de Vie. He renewed access to the spiritual teachings of Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross.

name: Saint Elijah
bio_en: The prophet Elijah is regarded as the spiritual father of the Carmelites. His zeal for the one true God and his experience of God at Horeb have shaped the spirituality of the Order.

name: Louis Martin and Zélie Martin (parents of Saint Thérèse of Lisieux)
bio_en: Louis and Zélie Martin, the parents of Saint Thérèse of Lisieux, lived a deeply Christian marriage and were canonized together as role models of holy marriage and family life.
